items.title: Iran Finds Escalation Is Fruitful Path to Leverage in War With U.S.
items.author: Yeganeh Torbati
items.content: <article>Iran and its allies now hold sway over two key oil shipping routes, and Tehran is setting the stage for a diplomatic win that could enhance its stature.</article>

items.title: Saudi Arabia’s Oil ‘Lifeline’ Was Attacked. Here’s What to Know.
items.author: Ismaeel Naar and Aaron Boxerman
items.content: <article>A drone attack from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to close its East-West pipeline, the kingdom said, threatening a key workaround to Iran’s Persian Gulf blockade.</article>

items.title: ‘We Left in the Clothes We Were Wearing’: Yemenis Flee New Fighting
items.author: Saeed Al-Batati, Shuaib Almosawa and Somini Sengupta
items.content: <article>Hunger and disease have tormented Yemen for years. Now, fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Iran-backed Houthis is pushing it to the brink.</article>

items.author: Michelle Goldberg

items.title: Why Mokha, Historic Port That Shaped the Coffee Trade, Is a Prize in Yemen’s War
items.author: Jonathan Wolfe
items.content: <article>A strategic location on the Red Sea afforded the city centuries of trading dominance — and makes it a coveted target in today’s fighting in the Middle East.</article>

items.title: Manhattan Bus Lane Plan for 34th Street May Be Stuck in Gridlock
items.author: Stefanos Chen
items.content: <article>Months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city would proceed with a redesign of 34th Street that had been halted by the Trump administration, the plan is no closer to completion.</article>

items.author: Ana Ionova and Edward Wong
items.content: <article>Officials say the Trump administration is blocking some of Brazil’s efforts to expand cooperation on fighting transnational crime.</article>

items.author: David Marchese
items.content: <article>In a new book, the writers argue that a powerful coalition of “end times fascists” is just fine with the earth’s demise.</article>
